Let F : C ⥤ Dbe a functor and let K be a Grothendieck topology on D. Then following SGA, III, 3.1, there is an induced topology on C: It is the finest topology making the functor F continuous.

Mathlib already defines "induced topologies" in two situations:

  • If C = Over X for some X : D and F = Over.forget X, then the induced topology on Over X is exactly docs#CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.over. This is fine.

  • If F is docs#CategoryTheory.Functor.LocallyFull, docs#CategoryTheory.Functor.LocallyFaithful and docs#CategoryTheory.Functor.LocallyCoverDense, then we have docs#CategoryTheory.Functor.inducedTopology. The covering families here are the coverings whose image generates a covering in D (in general, this does not give a topology, but in this special situation this simple construction works).

Now the problem is that mathlib's induced topology does not agree with SGA's induced topology, if F is not also docs#CategoryTheory.Functor.IsCoverDense: In fact, Functor.inducedTopology does not necessarily make F continuous (one can construct a counter example by playing around with the inclusion of WalkingCospan ⥤ WithInitial WalkingCospan).
Under the additional assumption F.IsCoverDense, SGA's induced topology agrees with mathlib's induced topology.

I think it is very confusing that we call something an induced topology that does not necessarily make the functor continuous. Therefore, I would like to propose to

  • rename docs#CategoryTheory.Functor.inducedTopology to something else (say Functor.restrictedTopology)
  • to introduce a new Functor.inducedTopology defined as in SGA.
  • to aim to use Functor.inducedTopology everywhere and add a lemma characterizing the covering sieves as the covering sieves of Functor.restrictedTopology in the case of Functor.IsCoverDense.

Opinions? (@Joël Riou, @Dagur Asgeirsson, @Robin Carlier might be interested?)
We should definitely not deviate from the literature! I'm strongly in favour.
Could you please rename the thread so that it's obvious from the title that it isn't about docs#TopologicalSpace.induced ? Thanks!

Kevin Buzzard said:

We should definitely not deviate from the literature!

I think the current definition, by Andrew Yang from 5 years ago, follows the Elephant, which calls this construction the "induced coverage" (and they call Grothendieck coverage what we call Grothendieck topology).
Does the situation where these don't coincide show up? (I don't know, could go either way)
My claim is no and when I have done the refactor, we at least know if it showed up anywhere in mathlib.
